title: The Periodicals run when work lands, and feed the look-first step
description:
## As asked

Repository: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** The Periodicals (Seams & Tangles, Drift & Coherence, Comprehension-Debt and the rest) are our independent check. They read the whole codebase without seeing our instructions, and this week they caught what the blind readers missed. But they run on a weekly floor rather than when there's something new to read. When they do run, they mint tickets into the queue, where pushed tickets tend to sit. On 4 November none of 17 pushed tickets moved, while all 4 findings pulled into work already under way were resolved.

**What we want.** The Periodicals run when work has landed in the areas they read, and the weekly floor stays as the fallback. Their readings go into the area notes (added earlier in this round), where the look-first step reads them, so a finding gets pulled in by the next change that touches it. That's John's design from 2 November (on main: `docs/plans/survey.md`, "Periodicals in this design"): they become the codebase's picture over time and the look-first step's map, rather than a source of queued tickets. A larger tidy they point to goes to a person as a size of move.

An area no ticket touches is fine. The Periodicals get round to it in time. Where they sit in autopilot's order matters: the same note puts them below real work, when nothing else is waiting, not ahead of it.

**Appetite:** err larger.

**Done looks like:** after work lands, the relevant Periodicals run without anyone minting them, and the next look-first step in an area they read cites what they found.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Implementation Plan

*Pruned at close-out (8 Nov 2026). The full plan, its revisions, research and design sections are kept in the task snapshots (*`GET /issues/LIN-4349/snapshots`*) and in the comment trail.*

**needs multiple sessions**. One session would lose track of three things: the 13-template test census against the fold's new state; the prompt-budget rebase against LIN-4369, which moves the same ceilings now; and the live proof run between P1 and P2.

plan-review due: yes. This revision changes the plan's trigger (the self-trigger fix) and adds the scoped tail. The plan needs more than one session, changes what autopilot dispatches and the published run-state contract, and loosens the Periodicals' minting contract on purpose.

## Implemented

The plan was implemented as approved in four pieces. There was one deviation, which was corrected.

* **P1, LIN-4379:** Seams & Tangles writes area notes and a report instead of tickets. It carries the source tag and citation contract, proven live by run 10 (LIN-4387, #2372).
* **P2, LIN-4380:** the other 12 corrective Periodicals feed the notes and mint nothing. Design & Interface run 10 (LIN-4391, #2378) proved it. Three advisory templates still report to a person.
* **P3, LIN-4381:** merged close-out events make a lane read `landed`, with self-exclusion of Periodical-owned merges.
* **P4, LIN-4382:** `AUTOPILOT_PRECEDENCE` owns the order (human goal, `due`, stack work, `landed`) and the scoped-run tail. Merged through `a478e5d9`.
* **Deviation, now corrected:** P4's tail always handed off via mint with `"autopilot": true`. [PR #2381](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2381>), merged as `9574d537`, makes an unbudgeted run drive its review in place and keeps the handoff only for budgeted runs. That applies the coordinator's call after ruling `lin4349-tail-spend` was withdrawn.

## Not yet witnessed (post-deploy checks, not run at close-out)

These are recorded for the operator on the close-out comment and on PR #2381:

* the unprompted scoped tail;
* no chain;
* a look-first citation of a reading-sourced notes entry;
* `design-review` self-exclusion, read after 9 Nov 2026 14:30 UTC.

Rollback if a runaway tail appears: revert `9574d537`, then `a478e5d9`.

Outside follow-ups: LIN-4389 and LIN-4390.

comments.body:
**Area notes from LIN-4347 (planned; plan-review pending).** Where the Periodicals' findings will go:

- One file per area at `docs/areas/<slug>.md` on main, with two parts: what's been learned, and what's waiting.
- The areas come from `docs/areas/areas.json`, the product's one area list. It moves there from `scripts/code-shape/areas.json`, and the code-shape tools read it there.
- A unit test checks that every waiting entry cites a file that exists in that note's own area, and that each note stays under a byte cap.
- Writing a note means a PR, so findings fed in after a merge pay a PR each.

## Survey open-0: LIN-4349 @ 110e35e05

**Why this will be difficult**

1. **Minting is how they're built.** `lib/periodicals.js` has two stages: Stage 1 mints a review task, and Stage 2 writes a `docs/reviews/` report, mints capped follow-ups and closes itself. `lib/periodical-report-gate.js` blocks Done until a comment cites a commit or PR. The shared-contract tests (`tests/unit/periodicals.test.js`) forbid file literals and a baked-in report location, so the LIN-1967 location-agnostic rule collides with a fixed `docs/areas/<slug>.md` destination. Changing the output means changing the scaffold, the gate and those tests, across 16 templates.

2. **Nothing dispatches them.** Being `due` is prose that autopilot reads at kickoff (`lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js`). `lib/periodical-runs.js` says LIN-1629, which owns the dispatch decision, was never built. The pieces exist: `lib/scheduler.js`, merged events in `lib/close-out-merges.js`, and `lib/github-pr-files.js`. Merged events carry no paths, though, and no code joins the three.

3. **"The areas they read" doesn't exist.** Every repo-scoped template reads the whole codebase, and none maps to areas. Firing them all on every landing means 16 runs per merge. Someone has to decide a template→areas mapping, and the code gives no hint.

4. **The order is precedence written in a prompt.** Kickoff ranks a goal first, then a `due` Periodical, then the stack. `docs/plans/survey.md` says the rank under the stack "has no such rank today". Adding it is a prompt change under the byte freeze. It also risks starvation: if the stack never empties, runs triggered by a landing never happen. Decide whether the weekly floor keeps rank 2.

5. **The notes are nearly full.** `runs-and-dispatch.md` is 6040 of 6144 bytes. The guard requires every waiting entry to cite a file in its own area, and every write needs a PR. So each run opens a docs PR across several notes, which can conflict with close-out writing the same notes (LIN-4374). The Periodicals must prune and distil, not append. That's a different job from writing a report.

6. **"Cites what they found" can't be checked.** `GROUNDING_BY_KIND` (`lib/prompt-formatters.js`) asks builders to read the notes, not to cite them. The done criterion needs a citation convention, or a source tag on each entry.

**What I'd do first**

Change what one Periodical produces before building any trigger. A trigger on today's contract just mints tickets faster, which is the failure this ticket describes. Take Seams & Tangles, which is already area-shaped. Make it a single stage that ends in a note PR (pruned to the cap, entries tagged with their source) with no follow-up tickets. Run it once by hand against the guard.

Then build the trigger: merged event → PR files → `docs/areas/areas.json` → mark the matching templates due at a new rank below the stack, with the weekly floor kept as a separate path. Extend to the other 15 templates last. "Err larger" fits: this is three moves (output, trigger, rank), and shipping them in reverse order fails.

## Survey global: LIN-4349 @ 110e35e05

**Where it lands.** Four parts that don't know about each other yet:
- `lib/periodicals.js`: 16 templates on one shared scaffold, with a two-stage contract whose whole point is minting tickets, and byte-pinned prompts.
- `lib/periodical-runs.js`: a pure ledger, cadence only, with per-`(periodicalId, repo)` lanes. Its header still names "LIN-1629's still-unbuilt dispatch decision", which is this task.
- The precedence order. It exists only as prose, in `lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js`, `docs/autopilot.md`, `docs/autopilot-kickoff.md` and `docs/architecture/source-map.md`.
- `docs/areas/`: three days old and well guarded.

The periodical code is getting better (LIN-4317 left one grant rule and one lookup).

**Done the obvious way.** A hook after close-out, an `areas` field on each template, Stage 2 told to write notes, and a new rank in the kickoff text. What that would do:
- **A sixth way to start a periodical.** The five today are Mint, Mint+Autopilot, the proxy mint route, `periodicalId`, and the cadence floor. Every entrance census and grant witness must learn it.
- **Findings in three homes.** `docs/reviews/` reports, `## Waiting` entries, and the follow-ups the scaffold still mints. `LEFTOVER_RULE` forbids an item living in two places. Unless the minting bullet goes in the same change, items will.
- **Areas inside the engine.** No `lib/` code reads `areas.json`; only scripts and prompt text do. The periodical contract test forbids file literals. Areas on templates would break the location-agnostic, multi-repo design.
- **Findings with no home.** Seams & Tangles reports cross-area seams. The note guard files each entry under the area of its first cited path, so the other side never sees it. Recent Headwinds reads the tracker, no area.
- **No room.** `runs-and-dispatch.md` is at 6040 of 6144 bytes, where most findings would go.
- **An order that fights itself.** A rank "under the stack" never fires while the stack keeps its Backlog, the 17 unmoved tickets included. "Nothing else waiting" needs a definition the kickoff can check.
- **Which look-first step?** Survey prompts get no area-note grounding (`GROUNDING_BY_KIND`), and survey-place forbids reading maps. If "look-first" means the Surveys, the done-check contradicts them. If it means the `WORK_IN_AREA` grounding, that is already wired. LIN-4370 should say which.

**Better, and within this task's reach.**
- Make landed work an input to the existing fold: a lane reads `due` early once a merge has landed in its repo since that lane's last run. That keeps one state and one entrance, and autopilot already reads it.
- Let each run find its areas from the diff since its last report. The engine keeps no registry.
- Change the scaffold once: drop "mint follow-ups" and add "write Waiting entries and Lessons through a PR". The report gate already accepts that PR's URL as evidence.
- Write the new precedence once and have the four docs point to it.
- Prune `runs-and-dispatch.md` in the same change.

**Better still, but not this task's.** A home for cross-area seams, either areas for docs and scripts or a pairs section in the notes. (a registry-shape change; LIN-3829 caution). And a precedence held in code rather than prompt prose.

## Size of the move (the person's call)

Err larger, John's standing answer. Both Surveys agree on the order. Change what a Periodical produces first, then what starts one, then where it sits. A trigger built on today's contract would just mint tickets faster, which is the failure this ticket is about.

**What John has already decided** (his design of 2 November, `docs/plans/survey.md`, "Periodicals in this design"): the Periodicals stop minting tickets into the queue. They become the codebase's film, meaning its trend over time and where each area stands now. They're the map for the look-first work, and they tidy in idle time. An area that no ticket touches is fine: the Periodicals get round to it in time.

**What a Periodical produces.** Its findings reach the area notes, so the next change in that area pulls them in. They don't go to the queue. The notes are small and near their limit, so pruning and distilling are part of the job. The film doesn't live in the notes. The reports in `docs/reviews/` keep the trend over time, as a record of a reading rather than a list of things to do. When a Periodical points to a larger tidy, it goes to a person as a size of move: offered when work next touches that area, or put to John directly. It does not become a queued ticket. Prove the new shape on one Periodical before changing the rest, and carry it to the others where it pays. Seams that cross two areas have no home in the notes yet. Say so; don't solve it here.

**What starts one.** Landed work makes a Periodical due sooner, as an input to the way "due" is already worked out. It is not a new way to start a run. Each run works out its areas from what has changed since its last report.

**Where it sits.** Runs triggered by landed work go below real work, as John's design has it. Define "nothing else waiting" so autopilot can check it, and make sure these runs can't be starved forever. The weekly floor stays as the backstop, where it sits today. If you think it should move, raise a ruling. The order is written in four places, so write it once and have the others point to it.

**The map.** Since 4 November the Surveys have read only the code, and that has worked. Scoping, which now decides the size, reads both the Surveys and the notes, so that's where the Periodicals' findings meet the look-first work. If you think the Surveys themselves should read the notes, raise that as a ruling.

**Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself, and record why. Raise a ruling only for John's calls: how big a move is, what's spent, removing a step, the order of work, and authority. Work that doesn't depend on a ruling keeps moving.

**Done when** work lands, the Periodicals covering the changed areas run without anyone minting them and below real work, their findings arrive in the notes rather than as tickets, the reports still show each area over time, and the next scoping or build in one of those areas shows it used a finding.

**Plan written (LIN-4349).** The full plan is in the description, under `## Implementation Plan`. No cuts to the As-asked block.

One question for John. It does not block P1 to P3:

DECISION: May a scoped autopilot run take one Periodical as it finishes? The rule would be: once its own task is done, before it stops, take one note-feeding or advisory lane reading `due` or `landed`, oldest first.
- **Why:** of the last 100 dispatches, all 3 autopilot rows were scoped, and `GET /periodicals` shows 11 of 16 lanes reading `due`, 2 to 2½ weeks overdue. So the rank under the stack in general runs (and the weekly floor at rank 2) is rarely reached. The tail is what makes "after work lands, they run without anyone minting them" actually happen.
- **Cost:** at most one Periodical run (two sessions) per finished ticket, and each lane runs at most once a day (`LANDED_MIN_GAP_MS`).
- **Authority:** it widens a scoped run's remit beyond its one task.
- **Recommendation: yes.** Without it, rank 4 is built for general runs only.

Yes, add the scoped-run tail in piece 4

— Ruling recorded via Harbour

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Request Changes. The plan is sound, but its self-trigger exclusion would not work in production, and no witness in the plan would show that.

Blocking findings: 1

**How it meets what was asked.** It delivers "after work lands, the relevant Periodicals run without anyone minting them, and the next look-first step in an area they read cites what they found", with no narrowing. The Done-when comes from John's size comment and matches the block. One part of that wording depends on John's open DECISION, which the plan correctly raises: will a scoped run take a lane as it finishes? Without it, "without anyone minting them" depends on general runs, and those are rare today.

**What I checked** (main is still at `110e35e0`; nothing has landed since the plan was written):
- `foldPeriodicalRuns` (`lib/periodical-runs.js`) is pure and has `now` injected. It works per `(periodicalId, repo)` lane, and its rule order is queue, then cadence, then never. Adding `landed` between "would be `recent`" and the queue/cadence rules fits that order without disturbing it.
- The template counts are right: 13 corrective builders call `mint()` (11) or `mintObjectiveBreakage()` (2), and 3 are advisory. Recent Headwinds is the only `scope: 'workspace'` template.
- `adversarialRead()` already gives Stage 2 the merge of its own docs-only PR. So "one docs-only PR, merged by the run" needs no new authority.
- The kickoff (`lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js`) has the two conflicting orders the plan names: the Orient step at about line 485, with 2 levels, and the general first act at about lines 720-728, with 3 levels. Today's text never names `POST /periodicals/{id}/mint`, as the plan says.
- Close-out events carry `prUrl`, `issueIdentifier` and `prMergedAt`. Since LIN-3756, `createPipelineMergeRecorder` records pipeline merges, but only on a proxy Done write and only with a GitHub token. So P3's pre-check is the right gate.

---

#### Blocking

**B1. The self-trigger exclusion depends on a field the route never reads.** The plan says to "exclude landings whose issue is named by any Periodical row". But `GET /api/proxy/periodicals` (`routes/proxy-compute.js`, about line 962) reads queue and history rows under `PERIODICAL_PROJECTION` and `PERIODICAL_HISTORY_PROJECTION` (`lib/dispatch-store.js:123-152`). Neither projects `issueIdentifier`. Every row would arrive with `issueIdentifier` undefined, so the exclusion would match nothing.

The plan's witness (risk 1) is a pure fold test that feeds rows by hand. It would pass, and production would still retrigger. Each Periodical's own report PR merge would mark every other repo lane `landed`. That makes a loop that keeps itself going, limited only by the one-day gap: up to about 15 lanes, at two sessions each, every idle day. If the scoped tail is approved, it would also run in the time after each finished ticket.

The projection's own comment records this same silent drop three times already (`followUpTo`, `abort`, `repo`).

*Change needed in the plan:*
- P3 adds `issueIdentifier: 1` to `PERIODICAL_PROJECTION`, which both projections share.
- P3 adds a route-level witness: seed a Periodical history row for issue X and a merged close-out event for X in the store, call `GET /periodicals`, and assert the lane stays `recent`. That test fails without the projection change.

One more point: the exclusion only works if the Stage-2 opening row is stamped with `periodicalId` and names the review task. That is how the kickoff's existing opening stamp works today. State the dependency, so that a later change to stamping knows it is load-bearing.

---

#### Notes for the builder (not blocking)

1. **"Stage 2 writes only its report" is a second behaviour the plan does not list.** Under "every place the behaviour lives", the plan lists the places that mint. Three other shared bullets would contradict the new notes contract:
   - `periodicalBullet.reviewOnly()` (used by Seams & Tangles): "no docs beyond writing the report artifact itself". This directly forbids the note edits.
   - `periodicalBullet.conclude()`: "The follow-up tasks you minted carry the actionable work forward … the highest-severity work is on the stack".
   - `periodicalBullet.gapAudit()`: "whatever follow-up work this review mints stays within its existing bound".

   The plan's census looks for instructions to *create* follow-up tasks, so it may not catch `conclude()` or `reviewOnly()`. In P1:
   - give `reviewOnly()` a parameter, or add a variant, that allows "the report and the area-notes edits";
   - give the converted templates a `conclude` that names the notes PR, not minted tasks;
   - reword `gapAudit()`'s bound;
   - extend the census so it also fails on "no docs beyond the report" and "follow-up tasks you minted" in a converted template.

   The advisory templates keep `concludeAdvisory()` and are unaffected.

2. **`landed` would also speed up the two repo-scoped advisory templates** (Stability, and Integration & Surface Maturity). The plan keeps them as reports to a person, not note feeders. Its `landed` rule is "any `scope: 'repo'` template", so 15 lanes qualify, not 13. If that is intended (the DECISION text says "note-feeding or advisory"), put the daily ceiling in the cost line for John: up to 15 lanes × 2 sessions per idle day. If it is not intended, limit `landed` to templates that feed the notes, and make that a property of the template, not a map in the engine.

3. **The order is spelled out in more places than the plan lists.**
   - `docs/autopilot-orchestrator-prompt.md` (about lines 66-70) lists the three ranks.
   - `docs/autopilot.md` §6 (about lines 170-191, 360, 368) restates them more than once.

   Point these at `AUTOPILOT_PRECEDENCE`, or mark them as historical (the orchestrator prompt is a "Stage B draft"). A cheap witness for the anti-duplication test is `grep -rn "past its cadence threshold\|overdue periodical" docs lib`.

4. **The kickoff text is under the prompt freeze too.** P4 adds rank 4 and the mint-route instructions, and removes one duplicate order. Re-measure the kickoff's ceiling in `tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js` after rebasing, and record the reason beside it. This is the same discipline P1 applies to `formatAreaNotesPointer`.

5. **Landings read failure.** "Read failure supplies no landings" needs a store method that can tell a failure apart from an empty result. The sibling reads in `CloseOutEventsStore` swallow errors and return `[]`, so an empty result already means `recent`. That is the fail-safe direction, so this is fine. Just don't copy `firstPressAt`'s throwing style without a reason.

6. **P3 pre-check, concretely.** For #2361 (LIN-4376), confirm that a `merged: true` event exists in the close-out events for this workspace, for example through `listForIssue`. If none exists, the cause is in `createPipelineMergeRecorder`'s preconditions: a missing workspace id or installation token, or the Done not written through the proxy. Note which one you find.

7. **Rebasing against LIN-4369.** LIN-4369 is moving the same budgets and the pointer reach. Settle P1's `formatAreaNotesPointer` sentence and its ceiling on top of whatever has merged by then, as the plan already says.

Once B1 is folded into P3, the plan is ready for `implementation` with the notes above.

**Plan revised (LIN-4349).** It takes in John's ruling and answers the plan review. The plan in the description was replaced in place.

- **Ruling:** "Yes, add the scoped-run tail in piece 4". It is built in P4, rendered once inside `AUTOPILOT_PRECEDENCE`. The LIN-1829 scoped byte-identity test changes on purpose. The cost line now states the ceiling: 15 repo-scoped lanes, one Periodical run per finished ticket in scoped runs, at most 15 × 2 sessions per idle day in general runs, and each lane at most daily.
- **B1, fixed.** Confirmed at `110e35e0`: `PERIODICAL_PROJECTION` grants no `issueIdentifier`.
  - P3 adds the field.
  - Risk 1 now has a route-level witness against the real store: a Periodical history row and a merged event for the same issue, with the lane staying `recent`. Without the projection change that test fails.
  - The plan now states the dependency on the Stage-2 `periodicalId` stamp and the gate-marker derivation, so a later change to either knows it is load-bearing.
- **Note 1, fixed.** P1 changes the wording of `reviewOnly()`, `conclude()` and `gapAudit()` for converted templates. The census also fails on "no docs beyond writing the report artifact" and "follow-up tasks you minted".
- **Note 2:** intended. The two repo-scoped advisory templates do qualify for `landed`; the ceiling is stated as above.
- **Note 3, fixed.** The places list now covers `docs/autopilot.md` §6 (every restatement) and `docs/autopilot-orchestrator-prompt.md` (marked historical, with a pointer). The search adds "past its cadence threshold". The dated session log stays as written.
- **Note 4, disagreed.** At HEAD, `tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js` has no ceiling for `lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js`; it names only `buildRunnerKickoff`. The plan says to re-measure if a ceiling exists after the rebase.
- **Note 5, fixed.** Follow the store's error-swallowing sibling reads, not `firstPressAt`.
- **Note 6, fixed.** The P3 pre-check now names #2361, `listForIssue`, the three preconditions of `createPipelineMergeRecorder`, and says to record which one is the cause.
- **Note 7:** already in the plan (rebase against LIN-4369 and re-measure).

Autopilot: aborted redundant plan dispatch c1144952. The original plan session (00c42e64) was resumed by John's ruling and already revised the plan answering plan-review B1 (comment at 10:00). A second concurrent plan pass would race on the description. Next: plan-review of the revised plan.

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Approve. The revision fixes B1 where it lives, and its new witness fails without the fix. The scoped tail matches John's ruling. What remains are notes for the builder.

**How it meets what was asked.** It delivers "after work lands, the relevant Periodicals run without anyone minting them, and the next look-first step in an area they read cites what they found" with no narrowing. Output comes first (P1–P2), then the `landed` state (P3), then the rank under real work plus the scoped tail (P4, John's ruling of 8 Nov). Recent Headwinds stays on the weekly floor, because it reads the tracker rather than code. That follows from the block's "in the areas they read", so it is not a cut.

**What I checked** (main is still `110e35e0`; nothing has landed since the plan was written):
- **B1 is answered, and the fix holds.** `PERIODICAL_PROJECTION` (`lib/dispatch-store.js:123`) grants no `issueIdentifier` today. `PERIODICAL_HISTORY_PROJECTION` spreads it, so adding the field once reaches both route reads. Both `_formatItem` and `_formatHistoryItem` already carry `issueIdentifier`, so the field survives formatting once it is projected. Stage-2 rows name the review issue and carry `periodicalId` in two ways: the kickoff's opening stamp, and `resolvePeriodicalIdFromGateMarker` (`routes/proxy.js:1568`), which stamps every recommend-and-dispatch on a gate-marked issue. The route's `periodicalEvidenceRow` filter admits exactly those rows. The merged event for that PR carries the Done-written ticket's identifier (`createPipelineMergeRecorder` → `recordMergedPrs`, `issueIdentifier: ticket.identifier`), which is the review issue. The exclusion therefore matches in production. The route-level real-store test is the right witness.
- **Note 4's disagreement is correct.** `tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js` has no ceiling for `lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js`.
- **The fail-safe direction is right.** `CloseOutEventsStore`'s sibling reads (`listForIssue`, `findMergedByPr`) catch errors and return `[]`/`null`.
- **The two conflicting orders exist where the plan says** (kickoff Orient at about line 485, first act at about lines 720–735). The LIN-1829 scoped block says "the precedence policy is moot … Do not pull other tasks off the stack", and the tail deliberately changes that.
- **The area-notes guard** (`tests/unit/area-notes.test.js`) checks only the *first* cited path against the note's area. So "area file first, report as second cited path" passes, provided the report is in the same PR (check 2: the path must exist).
- **Live `GET /periodicals`:** 11 lanes are `due` at 15–18 days, and all lanes are the default (null) lane, so "null lane matches any repo" covers today's data.

---

#### Notes for the builder (none blocking)

1. **P3: wire `closeOutEventsStore` into the proxy routes, and witness the wiring.** Today `createProxyRoutes` (`server.js:3263`) does not receive `closeOutEventsStore`, and neither does `createComputeRoutes` in `routes/proxy-compute.js`. The route has no events store to read. If the builder adds the dependency with a `null` default, the route-level test passes anyway, because it injects the store. In production, though, every read returns no landings, so `landed` never fires and nothing reports it. This is the same silent-drop shape as B1, and the fail-safe default hides it. Thread the store through `server.js` → `createProxyRoutes` → `createComputeRoutes`. Add a cheap witness that the server passes it. Either assert it in a test that reads `server.js`, as other wiring checks do, or log once when the periodicals route runs without an events store.

2. **A lane that ages past 30 days falls out of every rank.** With no evidence in the 30-day read horizon, the fold returns `never` (`lib/periodical-runs.js:270`, `:296`), not `due`. Today's case (2) takes only `due`. As written, the plan's rank 2, rank 4 and scoped tail take only `due`/`landed`, and `landed` requires "would otherwise read `recent`". Today's 11 `due` lanes (15–18 days) reach 30 days in 12–15 days. Any lane still unrun by then drops out of the floor the ask says "stays as the fallback". This also leaves a hole in the plan's "starvation is bounded by the floor". In P4, have the precedence leaf and the tail treat a repo-scoped lane reading `never` as the most overdue `due`. Add a witness: a kickoff/precedence assertion that names `never` beside `due`. This needs no fold change.

3. **The tail can read before the landing is recorded.** `recordPipelineMerge` runs fire-and-forget after the proxy Done write (`routes/proxy-writes.js:539`), and it makes GitHub reads first. A tail that reads `GET /periodicals` right after its own Done may still see `recent`.
